unit.title: Engineering a Deterministic Reaching-Definitions Analyzer
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student who knows at least one programming language and is building software-engineering practice
unit.topic_basis: The catalog explicitly names data-flow analysis within program analysis based on abstract interpretation.

included: control-flow graphs over a small JSON intermediate representation
input validation, stable output, tests, and engineering documentation
reasoning about convergence, joins, loops, and analysis limits
excluded: program synthesis, bug localization, and repair
reconstruction of the official PKU lecture order

learning_outcomes: Translate reaching-definitions equations into a terminating worklist implementation.
Keep mathematical analysis state separate from parsing, validation, serialization, and command-line concerns.
Produce deterministic results and safe failure behavior for malformed inputs.
Design tests that distinguish straight-line, branch-join, loop, unreachable-code, and invalid-input behavior.
Explain why a may-analysis result does not establish definite initialization.

required_evidence: learner responses to the comprehension prompts
unit_completion.passing_rule: At least 75 of 100 rubric points and every critical gate in the examiner-only rubric must pass.

course_completion.reason: This is one manager-authored kickoff drawn from a broad catalog description, not a verified official syllabus or a complete course sequence.
future_requirements: establish an authorized and provenance-recorded official unit sequence
prepare and validate the remaining theoretical and practical units
validate all required projects and cumulative learning outcomes
retain independent validator evidence for every promotion

provenance.authorship_note: The unit framing, task, comprehension prompts, and rubric are newly prepared learning-factory artifacts; they are not represented as PKU course materials.
